title: HTTP Lifecycle Plan Invocation Dry-Run Gate
summary: The FP-MCP-258 artifact-only HTTP lifecycle invocation dry-run gate was implemented, exposed, and verified against the persisted FP-MCP-254 lifecycle plan HTTPPLAN-20260703T233517042Z-9242deff. The gate reused the FP-MCP-257 plan validator, confirmed planReadable=true, planValid=true, sourceRequestReadable=true, planMatchesSourceRequest=true, lifecyclePlanReady=true, lifecycle tool binding=forgepilot_run_opencode_http_lifecycle_orchestrator, lifecycle approval binding=RUN_OPENCODE_HTTP_LIFECYCLE_ORCHESTRATOR, prompt and expected-text hashes present, and no prior execution/approval/contact/start/invocation state. It returned invocationEligible=true and invocationDecision=WOULD_BE_ELIGIBLE while all action fields remained false: wouldInvokeLifecycle=false, wouldCreateSession=false, wouldSubmitPrompt=false, wouldDeleteSession=false, wouldCallWaitEndpoint=false, wouldContactRunnerStartEndpoint=false, wouldStartOpenCodeProcess=false, and wouldConsumeApproval=false.
caveats: Dry-run eligibility creates no permission and performs no invocation.
The result is a point-in-time artifact observation, not a future authorization.
The dry-run gate does not call OpenCode HTTP endpoints; it evaluates persisted artifacts only.
A future real invocation path must still perform its own final preflight before any action.
boundaries: No runner start endpoint was contacted.
